summary.text: The Department of Veterans’ Affairs records Bernard Edward Shambrook, NX40242, as born on 1 September 1900 in Hertfordshire, England. He enlisted at Tamworth on 18 June 1940, from Wee Waa, with Winifred Shambrook as his next of kin. He was discharged on 23 October 1941 as a private in HQ Guard Battalion.
His service number appears in the notebook’s Tent 17 roster beside “A/Sgt SHAMBROOK B.E.” — acting sergeant. The DVA index gives his substantive rank at discharge.
An earlier AWM embarkation roll names Bernard Edward Shambrook, 2076, a 19-year-old butcher from Pimlico, Townsville, in the 5th Light Horse Regiment’s 14th Reinforcements.

birth.text: The birth details differ: DVA gives 1 September 1900 in Herts (Hertfordshire); the Virtual War Memorial profile gives 1 September 1896 in Herefordshire. The 1915 roll records age 19. The reason for the difference is unresolved.

context.title: Convoy US.10
context.text: AWM photographs identify Queen Elizabeth and Mauretania leaving Sydney in April 1941 in convoy US.10, with Île de France and Nieuw Amsterdam also pictured. The official naval history lists those four transports and Queen Mary.

context.title: The canal transfer
context.text: A 1982 Pioneer Battalions Association history names SS Ethiopia on the Port Tewfik–Kantara transfer in May 1941. It supports the spelling used in the reading copy of Bernard’s canal journey.

context.title: 7th Australian General Hospital
context.text: AWM photograph 022693 places the 7th Australian General Hospital at Kafr Balu, near Rehovot, helping locate the notebook entry.

context.title: Guard Battalion
context.text: The AWM holds a unit history for August 1940–October 1941 and a May–June 1941 diary under AWM52 8/4/1. The catalogue entries have been checked; the document pages remain to be examined for Bernard.

context.title: Cemetery notes
context.text: The Gaza pages bring together a 1941 heading, soldiers’ names and dates from 1917–18, and a sketch of the LIV East Anglian Division memorial. The heading’s month could be June or September.

overviewBiography.text: Bernard’s First World War record lists him as Private 2076, 5th Light Horse Regiment, 14th Reinforcements, joining on 18 October 1915.
The regiment belonged to the 2nd Light Horse Brigade, part of the ANZAC Mounted Division from 1916.
Virtual War Memorial Australia links this record to NX40242.

overviewService.text: His notes place him in the 1st Australian Corps Guard Battalion and list him as an acting sergeant on a brigade guard. They record guard duties and camp life within the Australian force in Egypt and Palestine.

warContext.text: The diary belongs to the Middle East theatre of the Second World War in 1941. Bernard travelled from Australia to Egypt and then into Palestine. His notebook names the 1st Australian Corps Guard Battalion and lists him as an acting sergeant on a brigade guard. These entries provide evidence of guard duties and camp service.

In North Africa, British and Commonwealth forces were fighting German and Italian forces and defending the approaches to Egypt and the Suez Canal. The siege of Tobruk began in April 1941, as Bernard was leaving Australia.

In June–July 1941, Allied forces, including Australia’s 7th Division, fought Vichy French forces in Syria and Lebanon, north of Palestine. The campaign aimed to prevent Germany establishing a presence that could threaten Allied bases in the region. Bernard mentions the Syrian armistice in his notebook. The pages transcribed here do not establish his personal participation in the fighting at Tobruk or in Syria.

The 5th Light Horse Regiment and ANZAC Mounted Division in the biographical entry relate to his First World War service. That regiment fought Ottoman forces in Sinai and Palestine. Its unit history describes the wider setting of that earlier service; it does not establish Bernard’s individual battle history.
